statement: Two actual boundary quotients on one open orbit, lifted through the same source universal covering, either satisfy F2=f F1 for a real-line homeomorphism f or form coordinates on a transitive open product-action domain. Explicit separate coordinate changes and a possible exchange identify that domain with the plane, the ordered-pair half-plane x<y, or the unit band x<y<x+1. Their full increasing coordinate-pair groups and all exact original covering equations are retained.
depends_on: C42 compatible lift construction; C43 connected proper-line fibres; verified Polish open orbit-map theorem; invariance of domain; explicit conjugacy of a fixed-point-free increasing line homeomorphism to unit translation
manuscript_passages: Section 23, folios 140-141, scans 279-281; Part C(b) infinite-operator request; simultaneous actual boundary-quotient constraints in the remaining extension problem
depends_on_doubtful_reading: None. Both target lifts are included in one closed Polish compatible group. The point-stabilizer inclusions prove the openness of the restricted maps and finite endpoint maps. Every domain change is written explicitly.
notes: The stabilizer of an F1-level acts transitively on that line and on its F2-image interval. In the nonconstant case the interval is open, the induced map is open and therefore strictly monotone. Constancy transports to all fibres and gives a continuous open surjection f of R. Otherwise the pair map is an open embedding with interval coordinate sections. Each finite vertical endpoint is itself an exact continuous open homogeneous quotient R to R, and hence a homeomorphism. Two finite endpoints have the same monotonicity; their fixed-point-free increasing transition is conjugated explicitly to translation. The global L-coordinate kernel is retained, and no original downstairs circle labels are fused. Additional third-quotient equations and global extension remain unresolved.
